data.name: Kshanvik
data.gender_notes: Kshanvik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kshanvik is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kshan' meaning instant and 'Vik' meaning power. This name signifies one who possesses the power to control moments in time. The name Kshanvik carries the meaning “Instants of time” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kshanvik usually hope their child will grow to embody instants of time and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the present moment with power and wisdom.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kshanvik total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: The Kshatriyas were the ruling class in ancient India, and the Kshanviks were a sub-group of the Kshatriyas known for their expertise in divination and astrology. They were considered the royal astrologers and priests who performed important ceremonies for the king and his court.
historical_references.context: The Hindu social structure was based on a caste system, and the Kshatriyas were the warrior and ruling class. The Kshanviks were a specialized group within the Kshatriya caste who were experts in divination and astrology.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, mentions a character named Kshanvik, who is described as a high-ranking priest and astrologer. He was a close advisor to the Kuru king Bhishma and played a significant role in the Kurukshetra War.
